baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the main operating values (design-point CP = 0.489 and CT = 0.804, 15 MW rated power, 20 MN-m rated torque, TSR 20→3, blade pitch 0→22°) and both repeat the same misread of the right-axis tick 2.25 as a rotor-thrust value at 10 m/s. Set B is the cleaner set: it binds Cp ≈ 0.5 to the Region 2 plateau (7–10 m/s) instead of a single wind speed, reads rotor thrust at 25 m/s as 0.9 MN (closer to the curve) rather than 1.0 MN, and repeats each fact far less often. Set A states the same facts up to three times (rated torque, TSR at 3 m/s, design-point CP, blade pitch 0° in Region 2) and gives mutually inconsistent rotor-thrust values at 10 m/s (2.8 and 2.25 MN).
baseline-first.remarks: Both extractions read the right-axis gridline label 2.25 in panel (b) as a data value for rotor thrust at 10 m/s; the actual thrust there is near the curve peak (~2.6–2.8 MN at the Region 2/3 boundary ~10.5 m/s), so the 2.7/2.8 MN claims are also only approximate. Both give Power Coef. ≈ 0.1 at ~17 m/s, which looks too low (the curve is nearer 0.2 there). Most quotes are bare axis labels and do not support the numeric values claimed — a systemic weakness of chart extraction in both sets. Both sets also omit the rated/region-boundary wind speed (~10.5 m/s) that conditions most of these plateaus.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts — design point CP = 0.489 and CT = 0.804, the Region 3 plateaus (gen. torque 20 MN-m, generator power 15 MW, rotor speed ~7 RPM), TSR 20→3 and blade pitch 0→22° — and both contain the same internally contradictory rotor-thrust reading at 10 m/s (2.25 MN alongside 2.7 MN in A, 2.8 MN in B). Set A is the cleaner extraction: it repeats far fewer facts (two duplicate pairs versus four in B, where TSR = 20 at 3 m/s, design-point CP = 0.489, blade pitch 0° over 7–10 m/s and generator torque 20 MN-m each appear twice) and gives the Region 2 ranges for CP ≈ 0.5 and CT ≈ 0.8 instead of only single points. Set B's only real advantage is a slightly better endpoint reading of rotor thrust at 25 m/s (1.0 MN vs A's 0.9 MN).
variant-first.remarks: Page is a three-panel curve figure with no data labels, so every numeric claim is a chart reading and every quote is only an axis label/legend entry; neither set's quotes can actually substantiate the plotted values. Both sets assert two different rotor-thrust values at 10 m/s (2.25 vs 2.7/2.8 MN) — the curve peaks near 2.8 MN at the rated point just right of 10 m/s, so 2.25 MN is the low/wrong one in both. Minor shared approximations not counted as wrong: rotor thrust at 25 m/s reads ~1.0 MN (A says 0.9) and power coefficient at ~17 m/s reads ~0.2 (both say 0.1). Both sets also miss the caption's attribution of the performance to the ROSCO controller, and both use the generic attribute name "value" for several claims.

baseline-first.note: Both sets cover all 15 rows of Table 7-1 plus the rated rotor speed and rated mechanical power, and both bind values to the correct rows and properties. Both contain the same two misread values (-82.60E+6 for the 18.0 m/s row instead of -83.94E+6, and -113.40E+6 for the 23.0 m/s row instead of -114.30E+6) and both repeat six rows as duplicate claims. The only differences are cosmetic (entity/attribute wording for the rated power and rated speed claims), so the sets are effectively equivalent in correctness.
baseline-first.remarks: Both extractions contain the identical fabricated values -82.60E+6 (18.0 m/s row) and -113.40E+6 (23.0 m/s row), which do not appear anywhere on the page; this suggests a shared upstream OCR/table-parsing defect rather than independent errors. Both also emit each of six table rows twice (11.4, 12.0, 17.0, 21.0, 22.0, 24.0 m/s), indicating a deduplication failure in the pipeline. Neither set captures the qualitative findings (sensitivity varies considerably over Region 3 so constant PI gains are inadequate; sensitivity varies nearly linearly with pitch angle) or the frozen-wake linearization assumption.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover all 15 rows of Table 7-1 plus the rated rotor speed and rated mechanical power, with identical bindings, units and conditions. Both also contain the same two misread values (-82.60E+6 for the 18.0 m/s row and -113.40E+6 for the 23.0 m/s row) stated alongside the correct values, and both repeat six rows as duplicates. The only differences are cosmetic wording of the entity/attribute labels (e.g. 'rotor | rated mechanical power' vs 'mechanical power | rated power'), so the sets are equally good.
variant-first.remarks: Both extractions appear to come from the same upstream pipeline: each emits the correct and an incorrect variant of the 18.0 m/s (-83.94E+6 vs -82.60E+6) and 23.0 m/s (-114.30E+6 vs -113.40E+6) rows, and each duplicates six rows (11.4, 12.0, 17.0, 21.0, 22.0, 24.0 m/s). The table is fully legible in the image; the text layer garbles the equations (7-16a/7-16b), but neither set extracted them. Neither set captures the qualitative finding that pitch sensitivity varies nearly linearly with blade-pitch angle (Eq. 7-16) or the frozen-wake linearization assumption.

baseline-first.note: Both sets cover the same core facts (filter type, corner frequency 0.25 Hz at the -3 dB point, 0.0125 s time step, and Bode-plot readings at 0.01/0.10/1.00 Hz), and both contain the same conflicting pairs at 1.00 Hz (phase -75 vs -80 deg, magnitude -12 vs -12.5 dB) where the quoted numbers contradict the stated values. Set A adds a third, invented phase reading of -72 deg at 1.00 Hz and leans on the figure caption as the quote for four plot-derived values, so its quotes support the claims even less. Set B is otherwise identical but has one fewer wrong claim and better-matched quotes for the plot readings, making it the cleaner set.
baseline-first.remarks: Both extractions read values off the Bode plot curves, which are only approximately legible; the -80 deg and -12.5 dB claims contradict the axis labels quoted alongside them (-75 and -12), and both sets state the 1.00 Hz phase and magnitude twice with conflicting values. The figure caption is used as the quote for several plot-derived claims in both sets, which does not actually support the numeric values. Neither set captures the state-space matrix definitions (A_d = alpha, B_d = 1-alpha, C_d = alpha, D_d = 1-alpha) present on the page.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover the same core facts (filter type, corner frequency 0.25 Hz at the -3 dB point, 0.0125 s time step) and both read the Bode plot at the same three frequencies, but each repeats several facts and states two or three conflicting values for the same point. Set A is slightly cleaner: it gives phase at 1.00 Hz as -75 and -80 deg, while Set B adds a third, -72 deg, whose own quote says -75. Both also state magnitude at 1.00 Hz as both -12 and -12.5 dB, and both use the figure caption as the quote for specific plotted values, which does not support them.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets leave out the discrete-time state-space matrix definitions (A_d = alpha, B_d = 1-alpha, C_d = alpha, D_d = 1-alpha) and the relation of the corner frequency to the blade's first edgewise natural frequency as a stated condition. Chart-derived values at 0.10 and 1.00 Hz are approximate readings from the plot and the text layer gives only axis tick labels, so exact values cannot be verified; the -80, -72 and -12.5 dB claims are contradicted by their own quotes (which say -75 and -12). Repeated claims (phase 0 deg at 0.01 Hz and magnitude 0 dB at 0.01 Hz appear twice in each set) suggest the extractor emits both a caption-quoted and a chart-quoted variant of the same fact.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in content, values, units and quotes; both correctly capture the drivetrain properties from the prose and Table 5-1, including the 5% critical damping ratio with its free-free-mode condition and the no-frictional-losses gearbox assumption. The only substantive difference is that Set A states the fully-deployed high-speed shaft brake torque three times (including a third variant 'High-Speed Shaft Brake | Torque | ... | conditions: Fully-Deployed'), whereas Set B states it twice. Both sets duplicate every table fact once under a component name and once under the turbine name, and both omit the DOWEC-derived supporting figures (0.35 MW loss at 6.25 MW aerodynamic power; 5,025,500 kg•m² equivalent low-speed-shaft inertia). Set B is marginally better for less duplication, with no loss of correct content.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets repeat each Table 5-1 row twice (component-level and 'NREL 5-MW baseline wind turbine'-level claims), a systematic duplication pattern worth suppressing in the extractor. Both also leave out the DOWEC comparison figures (0.35 MW loss at ~6.25 MW aerodynamic power; 5,025,500 kg•m² equivalent low-speed-shaft generator inertia) that justify the 94.4% efficiency and 534.116 kg•m² inertia. Note the prose calls the 0.6 s value a 'time lag' while Table 5-1 labels it 'Time Constant'; both sets follow the table label, which is acceptable but the two names are not reconciled.

variant-first.note: The two sets are essentially identical: both cover the same nine drivetrain properties with correct values, units, and quotes, and both keep the free-free-mode damping condition and the FAST/ADAMS no-friction-loss condition. The only difference is how the fully-deployed brake torque is phrased (A as attribute 'fully-deployed torque', B as attribute 'Torque' with condition 'Fully-Deployed'), which is a wash. Both sets state every fact twice (once bound to the component, once to the NREL 5-MW turbine), so both suffer equally from duplication. Neither captures the DOWEC comparison figures (0.35 MW loss at 6.25 MW aerodynamic power, 5,025,500 kg•m² low-speed-shaft inertia) or the driveshaft natural-frequency statement.
variant-first.remarks: Both extractions appear to be the same pipeline output with one claim rephrased; each of the nine table rows is emitted twice (component-level and turbine-level), inflating claim counts without adding information. Facts both sets omit: the DOWEC-derived 0.35 MW loss at ~6.25 MW aerodynamic power, the DOWEC equivalent low-speed-shaft generator inertia of 5,025,500 kg•m², and the statement that the driveshaft natural frequency matches the RECOFF model (no numeric value given on the page).

variant-first.note: Set B binds values to the correct elevations more often and captures the drawing scales for South Bedroom, North Bedroom and North Living plus the West Living MWL01 and 3'-9 11/16" segments with fewer invented bindings. Set A repeatedly attaches overall elevation heights to panel/label entities (W1 width 9'-11 1/4", "height P1" 9'-10 1/4", MWL01 width 3'-9 11/16", D1 width 3'-6"), puts 7'-6" on North Bedroom when that dimension sits in the West Bedroom (A3) block, and claims WB in the East Bedroom elevation where no WB appears. Set B's main faults are duplication (3'-9 11/16", the 1/2"=1'-0" scale and 9'-11 1/2" each stated twice), the misbound 1'-5 3/4" to North Living (it is in North Bedroom C5) and an unsupported P3 height of 7'-2 1/2". Both sets leave many dimensions under vague entities such as "interior elevation", "component" or "wall section" and omit a number of dimensions present on the sheet.
variant-first.remarks: The text layer runs in drawing order C1 North Living, C3 West Living, C5 North Bedroom, A1 South Bedroom, A3 West Bedroom, A5 East Bedroom; several of A's errors come from reading a dimension out of its block (7'-6" and 3'-6" belong to A3/A1 respectively, not to North Bedroom or D1). Both sets use bare dimension strings as quotes, so quotes give little evidence of which dimension line a value came from. Facts both sets miss include 13'-3 3/4", 2'-9 1/8", 9'-2 3/4", 3'-6 1/4", 7", 4 1/2", 9'-1 7/8", 8'-8 3/8", 9'-10", the F1/F2 and TV labels, D3 and P4; the artwork note explicitly defers size to the artwork package, so A's "artwork height 4'-3"" is unsupported.

baseline-first.note: Set B captures more useful engineering content — bolt diameter and length broken out, hex head type, adjustable footing type, CLEARVUE railing type, and the 2"X8" joist/frame correctly bound to the RAILING ATTACHMENT (C1) detail — while Set A repeats the joist/frame, grade-level and nail-spacing facts several times and includes tautological 'component = its own name' claims. Set A also misbinds the 8'-0" dimension to a generic 'deck connection' when it is the TYP. DECK MODULE (A1) dimension, which B states correctly. Both sets attach the 1'-4 3/4" spacing to the wrong context (A vaguely as 'deck connection', B explicitly as 'Detail C1' although that dimension string sits in detail A1) and both omit the A5 deck-to-house build-up. B's few errors are milder than A's duplication and trivial claims, so B is the better set.
baseline-first.remarks: Both extractions ignore the A5 deck-to-house connection build-up shown in the right-hand section: 3" STEEL DECKING, W10 X 15, 4-1/2" STRUCTURAL INSULATED PANEL W/ VAPOR BARRIER, CONTINUOUS WATERPROOFING MEMBRANE, 3" WOOD LAG SCREW WITH WASHER, and the 3/8" x 4" HEX BOLT there; the 4'-0" module dimension is also missed by both. The dimension string 1'-4 3/4" / 1'-4" / 1'-3 1/4" belongs to detail A1 (TYP. DECK MODULE), not C1, so B's 'Detail C1' condition is a misattribution and A's 'center to center' condition is unverified. Set A shows a clear pattern of restating the same fact under two names (joist/frame dimension x3, grade level x2, nail spacing x2, railing post bracket x2) plus tautological component claims.

variant-first.note: Set A captures more distinct, correctly bound engineering facts — bolt length (4"), bolt diameter (3/8"), hex head type, CLEARVUE cable railing type, adjustable scaffold footing type, and the 8'-0" deck module dimension — that Set B omits or reduces to trivial 'presence' claims. Set B does pick up one fact A misses (7/16" plate holes @ 12" O.C.), but it repeats the joist, frame, grade level, railing-post-bracket and nail-spacing facts two or three times each and adds self-referential 'component = itself' claims. Both sets bind the 1'-4 3/4" and 8'-0" plan dimensions to a vague 'deck connection' entity; A additionally mis-attributes the 1'-4 3/4" dimension to Detail C1 (it is in A1, Typ. Deck Module), while B mis-states 8'-0" as deck-connection spacing. On balance A is the more faithful and more useful set.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets ignore the whole A5 deck-to-house connection build-up shown in the text layer: 3/4" exterior plywood, 3" steel decking, W10 X 15, 4-1/2" structural insulated panel w/ vapor barrier, continuous waterproofing membrane, and 3" wood lag screw with washer — a significant shared omission. Set A also drops the 7/16" holes @ 12" O.C. spacing that B captures. The 1'-4 3/4" / 1'-4" / 1'-3 1/4" and 4'-0" / 8'-0" strings are plan dimensions of the typical deck module in detail A1, not 'deck connection' spacings; both extractors appear to bind bare dimension strings to whatever detail label is nearest. Text layer and image are legible; no administration content was used in judging.

baseline-first.note: Set A captures more of the page's real engineering content — the glass tile identity (FIRECLAY CRUSH "DANDELION", 2"x6"), the edge strip, the backsplash adhesive, and the D3 and D5 scales — while Set B drops all of these and instead pads with revision-history rows (admin, neutral) plus several invented conditions. Set B also misbinds the PT1 paint/finish code as a "PT1 substrate" and attaches an unsupported "Laundry Millwork Detail D5" condition to the 3/8" wall tile. Set A's main faults are one misread (treating the grid line "E" as a slope direction), a duplicated slope and duplicated wall-tile/PT1 facts, and vague entities ("drawing", "surface"). Both sets miss the 1/2" gypsum wallboard, 3/4" MDF gable w/ P3, steel L-bracket attachment and blocking.
baseline-first.remarks: The text layer flattens the D3 and D5 callouts into one run, so the single "3/8\" PORCELAIN WALL TILE" and "EDGE STRIP" strings each serve two details; attributions to a specific detail cannot be verified from the text layer alone (the image does show the wall tile in both D3 and D5). "PT1" is a finish/paint code, not a substrate or a named surface; both sets handle it poorly (A vaguely as "surface", B misbound as "PT1 substrate"). Facts neither set picks up: 1/2" GYPSUM WALLBOARD, 3/4" MDF GABLE FIN. W/ P3, STEEL L-BRACKET ATTACHMENT, BLOCKING AS REQ'D, and the "IN BRICK LAYOUT" tile layout.

variant-first.note: Set A binds the shower-pan buildup, substrate slope, glass tile dimensions and porcelain tile thickness correctly and with only one clear error (the 3/8" porcelain wall tile is attributed to Laundry Millwork Detail D5, when it belongs to the backsplash detail D3). Set B captures the D3 and D5 scales and the edge strip that A omits, but it introduces more defects: it reads the grid line 'E' as a slope direction, gives an unsupported generic 'drawing | scale' on a sheet that carries two different scales, and adds vague PT1 'finish paint'/'surface finish' claims. Both sets duplicate facts (slope, tile thickness, copyright/lot) and both omit the 1/2" gypsum wallboard, 3/4" MDF gable and steel L-bracket. On balance A is the cleaner, better-bound set despite B's slightly wider coverage.
variant-first.remarks: Both extractions leave out several labelled assembly items visible in the details: 1/2" GYPSUM WALLBOARD, 3/4" MDF GABLE FIN. W/ P3, STEEL L-BRACKET ATTACHMENT and BLOCKING AS REQ'D. The text layer drops the grid/zone letters context, which likely caused B's 'direction E' error; PT1 is a finish/paint key mark, so claims naming a specific attribute ('finish paint', 'surface finish') are speculative. Set A also repeats the same slope fact under two entity names and the lot number/copyright under both 'document' and 'sheet'/'project'.

baseline-first.note: Both sets extract the same layup materials and the CG/GC/NA/SC marker data from Figure 2-6, but B captures more of the marker coordinates (NA x2 and SC x2 in addition to the x3 values) while A states the NA, CG and GC x3 coordinates twice with contradictory values (0.05/0.1 m versus 0.0 m). B's only clear error is an internally conflicting CG x2 value (-0.15 m and -0.2 m, the latter apparently the GC value misbound), whereas A has three contradicted coordinate readings plus a 70%-span claim whose quote is only the figure title. Both sets duplicate every material under both "material" and "material layer" and both omit the Figure 2-5 lofted blade shape.
baseline-first.remarks: Marker coordinates are only legible to roughly ±0.05 m from the plot, so exact values could not be fully verified; the non-zero x3 readings (NA 0.05, CG 0.1, GC 0.05) are consistent with the markers sitting slightly above the x3 = 0 line and are corroborated across both sets, so A's 0.0 m restatements were treated as the misreads. The condition strings "Section : 0.7" and "cross section at 70% span" denote the same section and were judged as one fact, which is why each set's material/coordinate repetitions count as duplicates. Both sets miss Figure 2-5 (lofted blade shape) and neither records the x2/x3 axis units beyond the values themselves.

variant-first.note: Set A captures the full set of reference-point coordinates, including SC x2 = 0.1 m and NA x2 = -0.1 m, which Set B omits entirely, and its x3 values are internally consistent. Set B states the x3 coordinates of NA, CG and GC as 0.0 m while elsewhere giving 0.05/0.1 m for the same points, so three of its claims contradict its own others, and one cross-section claim carries the figure title as its quote instead of the caption. Set A's only substantive error is a conflicting CG x2 value (-0.2 m vs -0.15 m, the latter agreeing with Set B). Both sets repeat every layup material as both 'material' and 'material layer'.
variant-first.remarks: Marker coordinates in Figure 2-6 are only readable to roughly ±0.05 m at this resolution, so the exact x2/x3 values of CG/GC/NA/SC cannot be verified beyond the mutual agreement of the two sets (CG x2 ≈ -0.15, GC x2 ≈ -0.2, SC x3 = 0.0). Both extractions duplicate each material under two attribute names ('material' and 'material layer') and repeat the 70% span cross-section fact; neither reports anything from Figure 2-5 (lofted blade shape), which is only a caption and of little engineering value.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the text-stated gains (KP(θ=0°)=0.01882681 s, KI(θ=0°)=0.008068634, KD=0.0 s²) and the damping ratio ζφ = 0.7, and both read Figure 7-4 in essentially the same way. Set B repeats the erroneous 0.020 s proportional-gain-at-0° claim twice and gives 0.005 s at 25° where A gives 0.004 s, so B carries one extra wrong/duplicate claim; otherwise the two sets are near-identical. Both invent values at 25° even though the plotted curves end near 23°, both restate the θ=0 gains with off plot-read values (0.020 s, 0.007), and both duplicate the θ=0 facts under several names. Neither includes the gain-correction law GK(θ)=1/(1+θ/θK) or the previous-time-step implementation detail.
baseline-first.remarks: Figure 7-4's x-axis only spans roughly 0-23°, so every claim conditioned on 25° (three in each set) is unsupported; both sets treat the plot as if it extended to 25°. Both sets also re-derive the θ=0 gains from the curve (0.020 s, 0.007, 0.008, 0.0081) even though the text gives them exactly, producing conflicting duplicates. Quotes in both sets are mostly axis/legend labels that do not support the numeric values, and Set B additionally embeds values (e.g. "... 0.002 ...") that appear nowhere in the source text. Facts both sets miss: Eq. (7-20) GK(θ)=1/(1+θ/θK), the use of the previous time step's blade-pitch angle to compute GK for the next step, and the stated limitation that the simple gain-scheduling law cannot keep ωφn and ζφ constant.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the four-column LIGHTING LEVELS table and the Title 24 switch/vacancy-sensor requirements, and both repeat roughly the same facts with and without conditions. Set A's values all match the page, whereas Set B introduces two clear misreads: General Use/Movement stated as 5 FC (page says 3 FC) and the CFL equivalent stated as 5W (text layer says 9W). Set A does omit the 40W incandescent = 9W CFL = 7W LED efficacy example that Set B partially captures, but Set B only gets the LED half of it right. On balance Set A is the more faithful set because it contains no wrong values.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets duplicate nearly every table fact (with and without the activity condition) and use inconsistent attribute names ('lighting source' vs 'power source') for the same lamp-count row. Both quote the table header with typos ('CONRAST'/'CONSTRAC[T]'), which appear to be OCR/quote-layer artifacts rather than extraction errors. Both sets miss the statements that low-efficacy luminaires may be paired with vacancy sensors and dimmer switches, that dimmers vary energy consumption, and that the LED has higher efficacy because it emits more light per watt.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover the four-column lighting-levels table and the Title 24 switch/vacancy-sensor requirements, and both repeat every table fact twice (with and without its activity condition). Set A additionally captures the bulb-equivalence facts from the prose, getting the 7W LED equivalence right, while Set B omits both equivalences entirely. However, Set A misreads the CFL equivalence as 5W where the page says 9W, and Set B garbles the 'HIGH CONSTRACT' label as 'CONRAST' in one quote. On balance A captures more of the page's engineering content with one value error, while B drops two important facts.
variant-first.remarks: Text layer omits the graphic's LIGHTING LEVELS table entirely; all table claims were verified against the page image. The graphic itself contains the typo 'HIGH CONSTRACT' (for CONTRAST), which Set A reproduces faithfully and Set B mangles further as 'CONRAST'. Both sets miss: the definition of efficacy (light output vs. electric input), the statement that the LED bulb has higher efficacy because it puts out more light per watt, that low-efficacy luminaires may be paired with vacancy sensors and dimmer switches, and that dimmer switches allow gradual adjustment of light output/energy consumption. Both sets also state each table fact twice (once bare, once with the activity condition), inflating the claim counts.

baseline-first.note: Both sets cover the same five spanwise curves and share the same duplicated/conflicting pairs (prebend 0 m at r/R=0 twice, pitch-axis 50% at r/R=0 twice, twist 15.5/15 deg at the root, thickness 22/20% at the tip, chord 5.1/5 m at the root). Set A adds a clearly misread point (relative thickness 40% at r/R=0.25, where the curve is about 35%) and a misread twist of 0 deg at r/R=0.6 (curve is still slightly positive there), and its pitch-axis value at r/R=0.6 (30%) is less accurate than Set B's 29%. Set B also gives the closer chord peak (5.8 m near r/R≈0.25 versus A's 5.7 m), so B is the more faithful set overall, though only slightly. Both sets quote subplot captions or bare axis labels that do not support the numeric claims.
baseline-first.remarks: The text layer contains only axis ticks, labels and captions, so every numeric claim comes from reading the plotted curves; small reading differences (e.g. 5.7 vs 5.8 m, 37 vs 38%) are within plot resolution and were not all counted as wrong. Facts both sets miss: relative thickness is about 100% at the root (r/R=0), and the chord maximum is about 5.85 m near r/R≈0.22. Both sets repeat the same facts under near-identical wording (chord/chord length, -2.0/-2 deg, 15.5/15 deg), and several quotes are only subplot labels such as '(a) Chord length' or '(d) Prebend', which cannot support a specific value at a specific span.

variant-first.note: Both sets read the same five spanwise curves and share most claims, including the same near-duplicate pairs (prebend 0 m at r/R=0, pitch axis 50% at r/R=0, twist 15/15.5 deg at root, chord 5/5.1 m at root, twist -2 deg at r/R≈0.85) and the same self-contradiction of relative thickness 20% and 22% at r/R=1.0 (the curve sits at ~22%, so the 20% claim is wrong in both). A reads the chord peak as 5.8 m at r/R≈0.25 and the pitch-axis location at r/R=0.6 as 29%, both closer to the plotted curves than B's 5.7 m and 30%. B adds an extra relative-thickness claim of 40% at r/R=0.25 that the curve does not support (it is ~35-37% there; 40% occurs near r/R=0.2), and several of its quotes are only subplot captions such as "(c) Twist" that support nothing. Overall A carries slightly more accurate values and one fewer unsupported reading.
variant-first.remarks: All numeric claims here come from reading plotted curves; the text layer contains only axis labels and tick values, so no quote can literally support a curve-read value — both sets' quotes are weak by construction, and B's subplot-caption quotes are the weakest. Both sets also contradict themselves (relative thickness 20% vs 22% at r/R=1.0) and repeat several facts under slightly different values (5/5.1 m, 15/15.5 deg, 5.7/5.8 m), suggesting the extractor emits multiple samples of the same curve point. Both miss the root relative thickness of 100% at r/R=0, a conspicuous feature of plot (b). Curve-read values are approximate; borderline calls (pitch axis 30% at r/R=0.5, twist 0 deg at r/R=0.6) were treated as mild misreads where the plotted value is clearly off the claimed one.

baseline-first.note: Set A binds the louver counts to the operable screen bay and keeps the Flexinol force/temperature facts distinct, and its chart readings carry numeric values with the nickel-content condition. Set B repeats the 400 g, 2900 g, 2500 g, 15–20 C and louver facts under a misspelled "Flexnoll® actuator" entity, misbinds the 64/32 louvers and the 15–20 C Irvine range to the actuator, and misbinds the 2500 g wire load to the spring. B also emits two chart claims whose "value" is just the label "Ms °C" and gives two conflicting readings at ~50 at.% Ni (50 C and 0 °C). Both sets share the same garbled "cool force" quote and the unsupported Ms = -100 C at 53 at.% Ni point.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets quote "specified wire provided a 2500 gram force during the cool force"; the page reads "The specified wire allowed a 2500 gram force during the cool, martensite phase", so the condition (martensite phase) is lost and the verb misquoted in both. Both also claim Ms = -100 C at 53 at.% Ni, but the plotted data in the chart appears to end near 51.5 at.% Ni, so that point is likely invented; the chart is a scatter plot of literature data (Harrison et al., Han et al.) and single-value readings at given Ni contents are approximate at best. Set B's repeated "Flexnoll®" spelling is a consistent OCR/label misread of Flexinol®. Neither set captures the two mirrored independent assemblies per bay.

variant-first.note: Set B carries the same core Flexinol actuator and energy-load facts as A but without A's six duplicate claims repeated under the misspelled name "Flexnoll®", its misbound spring-force claim, and its two chart fragments that give "Ms °C" as a value; B also adds the supported trend that Ms temperature decreases with increasing nickel content. A's larger count adds mostly repetitions and label fragments rather than new correct content, and it also invents a 0 °C @ 50 at% chart point. Both sets bind chart-title quotes to numeric Ms values and both garble the "cool, martensite phase" quote as "during the cool force".

Both sets also miss the tool-chain facts (PreComp/VABS/BECAS computing stiffness matrices used in OpenFAST/HAWC2).

variant-first.note: Set A gives an internally consistent reading of the stacked bars: a thin glass_biax layer of about 3 mm on top of a medium_density_foam core whose thickness decreases from roughly 42-43 mm at SNL-FFA-W3-500 15% to 13 mm at FFA-W3-211 77%, matching the plotted bar totals. Set B instead attributes the large core thicknesses (13-42 mm) to CarbonUD, a layer with no visible black segment of that size, and states every web0 glass_biax value twice with conflicting values (3 mm and 4 mm). Set B also omits most web1 data that Set A captures. Set A is clearly the better set despite skipping the 64% and 100% span positions.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets quote stitched text-layer fragments (labels and percentages) that cannot literally contain the numeric values, since the values exist only as bar heights in the figure; this affects both equally. Exact bar values are only readable to within a millimetre or two from the image, so small discrepancies (e.g. Set B's foam 40/35/30/10 vs Set A's 43/38/33/13) were not counted as errors on their own. Set A omits the FFA-W3-241 64% and FFA-W3-211 100% positions entirely; Set B covers 64% and 100% for web0 but drops most web1 series. The circular 0%/2% columns appear to have zero or near-zero layup thickness and are unclaimed by both.

variant-first.note: A captures the sheet's key technical specs that B omits entirely: the 18'-0" solar envelope height, the 40-tube count for the 2 X APSE-20 collectors, and the 1/8" steel cable railing (material plus cable diameter). B is more careful with the window tags, correctly typing 1.07/1.06/1.02 as identifiers where A mislabels them as "dimension", and B also records both drawing scales. Both sets invent a PV-array grid-line location that the page does not state and both repeat the finished-floor, grade-level and handrail facts several times. On balance A's coverage of the substantive envelope, collector and railing facts outweighs its two misbound tag claims.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets miss POWDERCOATED STEEL FLATBAR RAILING POSTS, the D1/W5/W6 door and window marks, and General Sheet Note 2 (spacing may be larger between solar thermal tube arrays; necessary valves and piping not shown) and Note 3 (dotted lines = door swing, layered swing lines = tilt and turn) - note 2 is a real design condition. The PV-array grid-line location claimed by both sets is not resolvable from the text layer and only weakly from the image, so both claims are treated as unsupported; if the drawing does place one array over grids 4-5 or 4-6, that claim should be re-scored. Text layer contains the typo "TONNGUE"; A silently corrected it in one claim while quoting the misspelling.
